2. In Horayot, chapter 3, 13b, R' Meir was the sage and R' Natan head of the court. When Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, R' Meir, or R' Natan entered, everyone rose before them. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, “I want a distinction between me and them.” He enacted that when the nasi enters, all the people rise before him and do not sit until he says, “Sit.” When the court head enters, they make two rows for him, one on either side, and do not sit until he sits in his place. When the sage enters, one rises and one sits until he sits in his place. R' Meir and R' Natan were not there—that is, when the ordinance was made. The next day they came and saw that people did not rise before them. They asked, “What is this?” They were told, “Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel enacted this.” R' Meir told R' Natan, “Let us arrange something against this.” R' Natan asked, “What shall we do to him?” R' Meir said, “Let us ask him to teach us Uktzin, which he has not learned. When he does not know it, we shall say: ‘Who is fit to recount the Lord's mighty deeds? One who can proclaim all His praise.’ We shall remove him; you will be nasi and I court head.” R' Yaakov ben Karsha heard; see his entry. He said, “Perhaps, Heaven forbid, this will lead to humiliation,” and gave a hint that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel should study Uktzin. The next day they asked the master to teach Uktzin. He began and taught it. After he had established it, he said, “Had I not learned it, you would have shamed me.” He ordered them removed from the study hall. They wrote questions on notes and threw them in. What he could resolve, he resolved; what he could not, they wrote the resolution and threw it in. R' Yose said, “Torah is outside, while we are inside!” Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, “Let us admit them, but fine them by not reporting teachings in their names.” They called R' Meir “Others” and R' Natan “Some say.” They were shown in a dream, “Go appease Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.” R' Natan went; R' Meir did not, saying, “Dreams neither raise nor lower.” When R' Natan went, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel told him, “Granted that your father's golden girdle”—that is, a gilded belt, meaning the distinction of his father, who was court head—“helped you become court head; did it help you become nasi?”

Rabbi was teaching his son R' Shimon, “Others say ….” He asked, “Who are these whose waters we drink, but whose names we do not mention?” He answered, “These are people who sought to uproot your honor and your father's house's honor.” He said, “‘Their love and their hatred have already perished.’” That is, they have died; what place is there for this enmity? Henceforth it is proper to mention them by name: Rashi. Although R' Meir is said to have been alive at R' Shimon son of Rabbi's wedding, perhaps by the time R' Shimon son of Rabbi said this he had already died. He then taught him, “They said in R' Meir's name ….” Rava said: even Rabbi, who was humble, taught “They said in R' Meir's name,” rather than “R' Meir said.” End of quotation.

3. R' Yohanan said that the halakhah follows him wherever he taught in our Mishnah, except in the cases of the guarantor, Tzidon, and the last proof: Gittin 75a; Bava Kamma 69a; Bava Metzia 38b; Bava Batra 174a, see Rif there. There, 138a, Rashbam explains that this applies specifically in the Mishnah. Bekhorot 24a. Responsa Havvot Ya'ir writes: it seems to me there is proof from Ketubbot 109a. Tosafot, Bava Metzia 69, beginning of side a, require examination; Shakh relied on them in Ḥoshen Mishpat §171, subparagraphs 8 and 9 [the passage is at subparagraph 9 in the checked edition]. And Menahot 31 [the parallel citation in Ḥavvot Yair specifies 31b]. Rashbam, Bava Batra 133b, writes that Shmuel does not accept this rule, and neither does Rava; see Avodah Zarah 32b [Shmuel’s local ruling. For Rava, see Rashbam’s citation of 69b]. Rif, Bava Batra chapter 4, likewise writes that we do not hold this; Rosh, Bava Kamma 49a, writes likewise. See responsa Rashba, no. 40; Rosh, Ha-Sholeah 38; Ran, Mi she-Ahazo; Etz Hayyim's commentary, Ketubbot chapter 5 and 6:4; Tosafot Yom Tov, Eruvin 8:7, with a very lengthy discussion, and 6:1; and Bava Metzia 38b. Ketubbot, chapter 7, 77a: amoraim disagree about R' Yohanan's position, whether he accepts that rule. See Asheri, Ha-Mokher et ha-Bayit: the ruling follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel when unspecified, but where an amora disputes that ruling, we do not follow it. Tosafot, Bava Metzia 114a, s.v. Mahu: where the Gemara rules according to his opponent, the halakhah does not follow him. From there it seems to me proved that we do not follow Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, for there too it rules according to the sages against him; infer that it does not accept this rule. If you ask why, then, a ruling according to the sages was necessary, one may answer: because Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's reason is plausible; see Tosafot Yom Tov, Pesahim 4:5. Therefore R' Abba ruled according to him on R' Yohanan's authority. Rif, Get Pashut, likewise writes that where his reason is plausible, we follow Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. This requires examination, since Bekhorot 24a implies that everyone accepts this rule. See Sanhedrin 31a, where Rabbah bar Rav Huna rules that the halakhah follows him everywhere, even in the guarantor case and so forth. Sefer Keritut, Yemot Olam, gate 3, writes: R' Meir versus Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel—the halakhah follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Halikhot Olam, 34b, writes that the halakhah does not follow Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in tereifot. See what I wrote under R' Yehudah the Nasi about whether the halakhah follows his father against him.

4. Gelilot Eretz Yisrael writes that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is buried in Kefar Manda; see Akavyah ben Mahalalel. It is not known whether it is this one or Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel the Elder. Benjamin’s Travels is cited for the burial of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel at Kedesh Naftali [Adler’s edition places him at Almah, the preceding stop]; see R' Elazar ben Arakh.
5. Yuḥasin writes [citing the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon]: these were in his generation and reported in Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's name. Some of them, in my opinion, require examination:

Issi ben Yehudah was in his generation. R' Elazar ben Yehudah. In R' Elazar ben Yehudah of Bartota's name. R' Elazar son of R' Yirmeyah was in his generation; see his entry. R' Elazar son of R' Shimon was his pupil. ר״א בר׳ יוסי הגלילי [provisionally R' Eliezer son of R' Yose the Galilean]. R' Elazar ha-Kappar—requires examination. R' Elazar ben Taddai—requires examination. R' Berekhiah reports in his name. R' Zakkai disagrees with him. R' Zekharyah ben ha-Katzav: Rav Sherira Gaon writes thus, but this requires examination, for Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s father, Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, was young at the Temple's destruction, whereas this person lived in the Temple period. R' Hanina son of R' Yose the Galilean. Hanan ben Pinhas—requires examination; and Abba Hanan—requires examination. R' Hanina ben Gamliel was his brother. R' Hanina ben Hakhinai—requires examination, for he already had a daughter around the end of R' Shimon ben Yohai's wedding celebrations when he went to study Torah, whereas R' Shimon ben Yohai had already died when his son R' Elazar was before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, as is proved in Bava Metzia 84b: “Let one who has a father live”; see Rashi there. R' Yehudah did not come when he decreed a fast. In R' Yehudah's name: Tosefta Kelim, chapter 5. In R' Yehudah ben Yair's name. In R' Yehudah ben Lakish's name. R' Yehudah ben Gamliel was his brother. He said, “R' Yehoshua testified”: Sotah 48a. R' Yehoshua ben Korhah was in his time. R' Yohanan reports in his name. In R' Yohanan's name: Tosefta Kelim, beginning of chapter 4; but on that page it says in R' Yohanan the Sandal-maker's name. R. Yose Beribbi permitted him to sleep outside the sukkah [Sukkah 26a, cited here as “26 het”]; he permitted him treatment for toothache, see his entry, and reported in his name [pronoun antecedents require review]. R' Yannai reports in his name. R' Yaakov of Kefar Hittaya. R' Yeshvav the scribe—requires examination. R' Yishmael son of R' Yohanan ben Berokah. “R' Meir used to say,” and in R' Meir's name: Bava Metzia 106b. R' Mattyah ben Harash. Sumkhos. R' Akiva ben Dosa. R' Perida—requires examination. R' Pinhas ben Yair: Yuhasin writes thus. R' Pedat the Earlier—requires examination. Pelimo. R' Reuven Itztrobuli—requires examination, for he was old when R' Yehudah ben Bava was killed. In R. Shila’s name: Tosefta Kelim, chapter 1 [parallel at Kelim Kamma 4:9]. Shmuel reports in his name: Gittin 58a. R' Shimon ben Yehudah. In R' Shimon son of the deputy's name. R' Shimon ben Elazar disagrees with him. “I saw Shimon ben Kahana drinking terumah wine in Akko”: Tosefta Shevi’it, chapter 4 [parallel at 5:2]—requires examination. He reports three things in R. Shimon ben Beteira’s name: Tosefta Parah, chapter 11 [the parallel at 12:3 names R. Shimon ben Kahana].
